title: gpu-saturation-detection-and-eviction-playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft playbook for diagnosing and mitigating GPU pool saturation and noisy-neighbor style incidents in Dedicated capacity. Focused on: sudden GPU degradation (high utilization or memory fragmentation), one or more nodes causing disproportionate slowdowns, and autoscaler misbehavior when eviction/cordon/drain steps are needed.

Audience:
on-callers on SRE rotation, platform engineers who operate Dedicated GPU pools, and solutions engineers who need quick mitigation steps.

Quick summary / TL;DR (for pager):
- If a Dedicated GPU pool alert fires (High GPU Utilization or Long Inference Latency): query per-node GPU metrics and check for 1-2 nodes with >85% utilization while cluster avg <60% — likely noisy neighbor.
- If noisy node(s) found: cordon -> live-evict offending pods -> restart node GPU daemon -> uncordon. If eviction fails, power-cycle via host / cloud provider.
- If autoscaler is mis-scaling due to config mismatch: pause autoscaler, scale out manually to safety buffer, then fix scale policies.

Detection checks (PromQL examples / metrics to run on-call):
- Per-node GPU util: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent{pool=\"dedicated-gpu-1\"}[2m]) by (instance)
- Per-node GPU memory used / total: (nvidia_gpu_memory_used_bytes / nvidia_gpu_memory_total_bytes) * 100 by (instance)
- Inference queue depth: sum(inflight_requests{route=~\"/v1/.*\"}) by (node)
- Long tail latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(response_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

Red flags (indicate noisy neighbor or kernel-level issue):
- GPU util > 90% on 1-3 nodes while pool median < 50%
- GPU memory fragmentation (frequent allocation failures/errors in application logs)
- PCIe error counters increasing: nvidia_smi_dmon_pci_errors_total > baseline
- One host has significantly higher PCI bus or NVLINK retries

Immediate on-call actions (ordered):
1) Acknowledge pager in Slack and Post a short blurb in #sre-dedicated: \"Investigating Dedicated GPU pool alert — running per-node checks.\"
2) Run detection checks above and paste top 5 lines of per-node util in Slack.
3) If one node is the outlier: cordon the node (kubectl cordon <node>) and shift new pods away.
   Command: kubectl cordon <node>  # prevents new scheduling
4) Identify offending pods on that node: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
5) Live-evict safety-first: try kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=30 --wait=false for non-critical inference pods. For internal scheduler-critical pods, scale down replicas via deployment/RS.
6) Restart GPU daemonset / driver on host (preferred) before full reboot: ssh node -> sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker || sudo systemctl restart nvidia-device-plugin
7) Observe GPU metrics for 3–5 minutes. If util drops and latency improves, uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>. If not, reboot host or request cloud host reset.
8) If offending process is not a Redwood pod (customer VM or third-party process on host): escalate to infra on-call and provider support with node ID and PCIe logs.

Eviction caveats and safety notes:
- Do not drain stateful pods without explicit owner approval (cache servers, local KV).
- For inference pods with large KV caches, use rolling restart script that preserves warmup where possible. Example: patch deployment to replicas=0? No — prefer pod-by-pod kill + warmup wait.
- If draining causes autoscaler to see rapid pod terminations and scale-downs, pause autoscaler: kubectl annotate deployment <name> autoscaler.k8s.io/paused=true (cluster-autoscaler integration) or use infra tooling to freeze scaling temporarily.

Autoscaler misconfig scenarios we've seen:
- Vertical scaling bug: scale-up triggers too late because max-unready is set low -> backlog accumulates -> tail latency rockets.
- Label mismatch: new instances spin up in wrong pool (spot vs reserved) -> incompatible GPU drivers -> pods fail to bind -> autoscaler keeps retrying.
- Health-check false negatives causing aggressive termination.

Fix for autoscaler mis-scaling (short-term):
1) Pause autoscaler via infra console or annotation.
2) Manually add capacity with policy-compliant instance type as emergency buffer.
3) Fix offending scaling policy (thresholds, warmup, max-unready) in infra repo and roll PR for hotfix.
4) Resume autoscaler and monitor.

Post-incident RCA template (to fill after mitigation):
- Incident start / end timestamps
- Symptoms observed (metrics & logs)
- Affected customers & SLA impact
- Root cause hypothesis (noisy neighbor kernel, model batch spike, misconfigured autoscaler rule)
- Remediation steps executed
- Permanent fixes and owners (e.g., enforce per-pod GPU quotas, change autoscaler warmup, implement eviction protection for hot-state pods)
- Action items & due dates

On-call debug commands (crib sheet):
- List GPU devices on node: ssh node 'nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,ERRORS'
- Quick GPU utilization from prometheus-curl: curl "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent{instance=\\\"<node>\\\"}[2m])"
- Show pods on node: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- Kill pod gracefully: kubectl delete pod <pod> --grace-period=30
- Drain node preserving local storage (be careful): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force (only as last resort)

Playbook TODOs (open items / experiments to run):
- [ ] Implement pod-level GPU soft-quota admission controller to prevent a single pod from monopolizing multiple GPUs on multi-GPU hosts (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-01)
- [ ] Add a Prometheus alert rule for \"per-node divergence\" defined as nodes with util >85% while pool-avg <60% (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Create a small canary job that intentionally produces noisy-kernel behavior in staging to validate eviction and node-recovery path (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Document exact eviction side-effects for Redis/kv caches and create safe-drain playbook for those stateful pods (owner: Maya)

Unresolved questions / hypotheses (notes to self):
- Are we seeing GPU memory fragmentation from our model runtime (custom allocators) or from unexpected host processes? Need to correlate driver-level allocation failure logs with pod container logs.
- Do current instance images include a kernel patch that correlates with PCIe retry spikes seen in last 2 incidents?
- Can the autoscaler be taught to detect \"noisy node\" pattern and prefer scheduling new pods away from nodes with high steal/err metrics?

After-action checklist (immediately after incident):
- Open a postmortem doc and populate RCA template above
- Tag all related alerts, logs, traces in the incident ticket
- Add to next SRE on-call rotation agenda: 10-minute walk-through of the incident and the new alert rule (owner: Maya)
- Push hotfix or PRs for any config changes with link back to postmortem

Appendix: useful links and snippets
- Example autoscaler annotation to pause: kubectl annotate deployment <d> cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/paused=true
- Quick node metadata for provider support: curl http://metadata.internal/compute/instances/<node>/status
- Link to existing infra PR about eviction-safety: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789
- Relevant Jira: JIRA-SRE-4521 (investigate gpu saturation pattern, Sep 2025 incident)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep playbook short and actionable. The team hates 15-step docs at 2am. Emphasize the cordon -> evict -> restart -> observe loop.
- Next iteration: add a runbook script that does safe_eviction.sh and records all outputs automatically to incident ticket.

End of draft.
